dialog.body: Public Works, this is Kevin.
Hi, yeah, Kevin, my name's Bruce Gardiner. I'm calling about a drain problem at my mother's place. Can you hear me okay? I'm on my cell and the reception in here is lousy.
I can hear you fine so far. Go ahead, Bruce. What's going on with the drain?

So it's the catch basin, the one at the edge of the lane in front of her house. It's one eighty-five Kingston Avenue, up the Historic Hill. There's a snowbank piled right on top of it, from when the plow came through, and now the water just sits there. It spreads right across the lane.
Okay, one eighty-five Kingston Avenue. Snowbank sitting on the catch basin, water pooling across the lane. Got it. Is this from a storm, or has it been dry out?
No, no storm. That's the thing. It's been dry for days. It's just the melt off the bank, and it's got nowhere to go because the grate's buried. [line breaks up] ...and it keeps doing it.
Sorry, you broke up on me there. You said it keeps doing it?
Yeah, it keeps doing it. Every time it thaws a little during the day, then it freezes at night. My mother's got ice across the whole bottom of her driveway apron now.
Ugh, yeah, that'll be a skating rink. Have you or she tried to clear anything off it?

I did, Sunday. I went over and pulled the leaves off the grate by hand, because there was a mat of wet leaves in there too. And it helped, I'll give it that. For about ten minutes the water went down. Then it backed right up again. So I said to my mother, that's not the leaves, something's wrong down there, and she said, well, call the city, so here I am.
Okay. So leaves cleared by hand, drained for about ten minutes, then backed up again. That points to either the snow blocking it or something further down the line. Writing that down.

Right. And I'll be honest, I don't think this is the first time. She told me the guy before her, I mean the neighbor, said he'd called about it too, and nobody ever came. That's what she said to me. So I'd like somebody to actually look at it this time.

Understood. I don't have a record in front of me for that neighbor, but I'll put this in as a request for an inspection of the catch basin. Public Works would send somebody out to look at the basin and see if it's clogged or if the pipe's the problem.
So who do I call to get it checked? Is that you, or is there another number I should be using?

It's me, you're in the right place. I'm putting it in the system now, and the crew supervisor will see it. Sometimes they dig the snow off first and then check the pipe. It's probably a few days, maybe into next week depending on how backed up they are.

A few days. Okay. I just don't want it to turn into a sheet of ice, because she's, you know, she goes out for the mail and I worry. Sorry, I'm in a waiting room at the car dealership, they've got my car in for service, and there's a TV going. Hang on, let me step over by the window.
No problem, take your time.
Okay, that's better. Can you hear me?
Much better. Do you want the crew to call you or your mother if they need to get at the basin?
Me. Call me. Four oh one, five five five, zero one eight nine.
Four oh one, five five five, zero one eight nine. Bruce Gardiner, one eighty-five Kingston Avenue, catch basin blocked by a snowbank, water across the lane, no storm. Did I get it?
That's it. And put in the part about the leaves, that I cleared them and it only helped for ten minutes.
Already in there. If it gets worse before they get out, like the ice spreading into the lane, call back and I'll flag it again.
Okay. I will. Thanks, Kevin. I appreciate it.
You got it, Bruce. Hope the car's not too bad.
